## Document & Proposal Generation Workflow

Starter template from agentmelt.com — configure before running:

1. Fill in "Config (edit me)" (name, approver, quiet hours; test_mode stays on for the first week).
2. Add credentials to every service node (Anthropic, mail, CRM, database…).
3. Replace placeholder URLs, queries and field mappings with yours.
4. Set the trigger: A 'new proposal' form, a deal moving to the proposal stage in the CRM, or an RFP document uploaded to a folder starts the run.
5. Keep the gates: 'Needs a person?' after every AI step, 'Approved?' after the approval — wire their dead ends to a sheet or a channel.
6. Keep the guardrails:
   - Every reused answer is sourced to the document it came from; the writer can see what was adapted.
   - Commitments the rules forbid (uncapped liability, guaranteed outcomes) are blocked, not merely flagged.
   - Pricing comes from rules and rate cards; the agent cannot invent a number.
   - Nothing is sent to a client automatically; the workflow produces a draft for people.

Full blueprint and pricing: https://agentmelt.com/workflows/document-generation-automation/
Want it built and run for you? $247/month · custom $4,000–7,000 one-time

Fill these in once; every later node reads them as $('Config (edit me)').item.json.config.*

test_mode = true: log what the workflow would write, without writing it, for the first week.
approval_mode = true: the approval node waits for a person; switch off per message type once it has earned it.

Also point the nodes at your own sources:
- CRM (HubSpot, Salesforce) client and deal records
- Answer library: past proposals, RFP responses, case studies, security answers
- Document templates (Google Docs / Word)
- Pricing rules and rate cards
- Brand and legal rules (forbidden commitments, required clauses)

options.systemMessage:
You are the "Draft each section" step of the Document & Proposal Generation Workflow workflow run by Agentmelt.
Task: Section by section in your template: adapts the best past answer to this client's context, inserts CRM facts, applies pricing rules, and marks anything it could not source as a decision for the writer. Tone and format rules enforced.

Rules:
- Every reused answer is sourced to the document it came from; the writer can see what was adapted.
- Commitments the rules forbid (uncapped liability, guaranteed outcomes) are blocked, not merely flagged.
- Pricing comes from rules and rate cards; the agent cannot invent a number.
- Nothing is sent to a client automatically; the workflow produces a draft for people.
- Answer only from the data provided in the input. If something is missing, say so in the output instead of guessing.
- If this step produces a message or a document, put the full text in `draft` (and a `subject` if it is an email); put a one-line summary in `summary`.
- Set `needs_human` true whenever you are unsure, the input is unusual, or a rule above applies; a person will look at it.
- Return valid JSON matching the output schema; no prose outside the JSON.

Consistency and compliance check

Client name and figures consistent throughout, required sections present, forbidden commitments absent, pricing arithmetic correct, page and word limits respected.

nodes.name: Google Docs: Produce the document
nodes.notes:
Produce the document

Generated in Google Docs or Word from the template with styles, tables and the decision list at the top; PDF export on approval.

nodes.name: Slack approval: Route for review and learn
nodes.notes:
Route for review and learn

The writer and the account owner review; approved sections are written back to the answer library with the client context, so the next document starts from better material.

Send-and-wait: the run pauses here until someone presses Approve or Reject. Set config.approver in "Config (edit me)".

nodes.name: Approved?
nodes.notes: True = approved → continue to the write-back. False = rejected → stop here; the item stays where it was.

nodes.name: Rejected: Route for review and learn
nodes.notes: Rejected by the approver. Nothing is written. Optionally log the rejection to your sheet so the weekly count of corrections is visible.
